source.name: FAO Global Soil Salinity Assessment
source.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

cadence: Refresh when FAO publishes a successor global salt-affected-soils assessment or Global Soil Salinity Map.
provenance: Official FAO global assessment and Global Soil Partnership summaries. Current mapped area, affected land share, annual crop-production cost, annual land removed from production and population context are retained as separate source-reported quantities.
uncertainty: The 2024 global map combines heterogeneous national inventories, remote sensing, soil surveys and models. Natural salinity and human-induced salinization are not fully separable everywhere. The annual land-loss and crop-cost estimates come from earlier assessment syntheses and are not a current observation series. Irrigated-land and population exposure do not imply uniform yield loss.
failure_behavior: Retain the last reviewed assessment and mark stale. Reject changed area, currency, annualization, land or salinity boundaries. Never treat all salt-affected land as human-caused, distribute a global burden uniformly, score the additional area at risk as already affected, or fill missing uncertainty with zero.

assessment.geographic_scope: Global land assessment with salt-affected soils on all continents and explicit irrigated and rainfed cropland estimates

source_locators.biophysical_burden: FAO 2024 release: 1,381 million hectares, or 10.7 percent of global land, are salt-affected.
source_locators.human_economic_burden: FAO Global Soil Partnership: global annual cost of salt-induced land degradation in irrigated areas is estimated at US$27.3 billion in lost crop production.
source_locators.persistence: FAO Global Soil Partnership: salinization takes up to 1.5 million hectares of farmland out of production each year.
source_locators.extent: FAO Global Soil Partnership: salt-affected soils occur on all continents; the 2024 assessment reports global irrigated and rainfed cropland shares.
source_locators.human_context: FAO Global Soil Partnership 2021 map release: more than 1.5 billion people face significant food-growing challenges associated with saline irrigated soils.

excluded_from_scoring: one billion additional hectares at risk, which is not added to currently affected area
upper-bound crop-yield losses in the most affected countries, which are not a global mean
population challenge context, which is retained but not added to the monetary burden
